title: Kenyan Egg Stew
community: Enjoyed across all Kenyan communities — a beloved quick meal
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Egg Stew — eggs poached directly in a fragrant tomato, onion, and garlic sauce until perfectly set. Quick, nourishing, affordable, and deeply satisfying — one of Kenya's most beloved everyday meals. Ready in 30 minutes and loved by the whole family.
longDesc: Egg stew is the Kenyan kitchen at its most resourceful and most satisfying. A rich tomato sauce is built in minutes, then eggs are cracked directly into the sauce and poached until the whites are set and the yolks are still slightly runny. The yolk breaks into the sauce as you eat, enriching it further. Scooped with ugali or chapati, it is one of the most complete and comforting meals in the Kenyan repertoire.
steps: Heat oil in a large wide pan over medium heat.
Cook onions until soft and golden — 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8—10 minutes until a thick sauce forms.
Add curry powder and paprika. Stir 30 seconds.
Add water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Make 6 small wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover and cook for 5—8 minutes until the egg whites are set but yolks are still slightly runny.
Serve immediately — directly from the pan.
chefTips: The sauce should be thick before you add the eggs — a thin sauce produces uneven poaching.
Do not stir after adding the eggs — let them poach undisturbed.
A wide pan allows more eggs to cook evenly without crowding.
Cover while the eggs cook — the trapped steam sets the tops of the whites without flipping.
commonMistakes: Thin sauce — eggs spread too much and cook unevenly.
Stirring after adding eggs — breaks the yolks prematurely.
Overcooking — the yolks become hard and the dish loses its characteristic richness.

faqs.q: Can I use hard-boiled eggs instead?
faqs.a: Yes — see KEN092 (Egg Curry) which uses pre-boiled eggs in a similar sauce. The poaching method here is faster and produces a more integrated, saucier result.

faqs.q: How do I know when the eggs are done?
faqs.a: The white should be completely set and opaque — press gently with the back of a spoon to check. The yolk should have a slight jiggle for a runny result. Cover for the final 2 minutes for firmer yolks.

cookingScience: Poaching eggs in tomato sauce is essentially the same as poaching in water — the proteins in the egg white denature and coagulate as they heat. Tomato sauce conducts heat efficiently and adds flavour compounds that infuse the white as it sets. The acidity of the tomatoes also helps the egg white coagulate more quickly.
sustainabilityTips: One of the most affordable and lowest-impact protein meals available.
storage: Best eaten immediately — eggs change texture when refrigerated in sauce.
reheating: Not recommended — the eggs overcook when reheated.
healthBenefits: Tomatoes provide lycopene and vitamin C.
culturalNote: Egg stew is one of the most universally beloved meals in Kenya — quick, affordable, and satisfying at any time of day. From breakfast in a Nairobi apartment to lunch in a Western Kenya homestead, mayai ya mchuzi is a constant across the country.
regionalVariations: Spicy egg stew with extra chilli.
